decisions.rationale: The extract appears at the declared offsets and states that Harrison was grudgingly helped by Lennon while writing “Taxman.” It also states that Lennon suggested naming Harold Wilson and Edward Heath, the first living people directly named in a Beatles song.

The extract appears at the declared offsets and states that no Beatles played on the record. It further states that a closely miked string octet was recorded in 14 takes before Paul overdubbed lead vocals.
The extract appears at the declared offsets and states that recording began on 27 April 1966 with 11 rhythm-track takes. It also states that John Lennon added lead vocals two days later.

The extract appears at the declared offsets and states that after the sitar motif on “Norwegian Wood,” “Love You To” was The Beatles’ first full attempt at classical Indian-style music. The claim restates that narrowly.

The extract appears at the declared offsets and describes the lyric structure as combining the whole title, with verses addressing “here,” “there,” and then “everywhere.” The claim follows the extract without adding unsupported detail.

The extract appears at the declared offsets and says Donovan suggested one couplet after McCartney played him a yellow-submarine song and said a line was missing. It gives the “Sky of blue and sea of green/In our yellow submarine” couplet, matching the claim.

The extract appears at the declared offsets and states that “She Said She Said” was the final track recorded for Revolver. It also says the song was inspired by an LSD-influenced conversation between John Lennon and Peter Fonda.

The extract appears at the declared offsets and states that George Martin added a piano solo to track two, which also had all four Beatles’ handclaps. It also states the solo was recorded at half speed so it played back faster and higher.

The extract appears at the declared offsets and states that “And Your Bird Can Sing” is notable mainly for cryptic lyrics and twin guitar riffs. It identifies the riff players as Paul McCartney and George Harrison, as the claim says.
The extract appears at the declared offsets and says George Martin wrote down the understated melody Paul sang to him. It also states that Alan Civil performed it, matching the claim.

The extract appears at the declared offsets and contrasts the Robert Fraser belief with the statement that the song was actually about Dr Robert Freymann. It also states that Freymann ran a discreet clinic on Manhattan’s East 78th Street.

The extract appears at the declared offsets and is attributed to George Harrison. It says the chord was an E7th with an F on top played on piano and that Harrison was proud because he literally invented it.

The extract appears at the declared offsets and states that The Beatles hired two members of Georgie Fame’s group The Blue Flames. It also says John Lennon and Paul McCartney knew them from the London club scene.

The extract appears at the declared offsets and states that “Tomorrow Never Knows” was the monumental closing track on Revolver. It also says it was the first song recorded for the album, which directly supports the claim.
